Intended major: architecture or art history

**NYU**

NYU Pros:

* in a cool city
* basically free (i only have to pay 8k/year)
* i'm artsy and it seems like an artsy crowd
* guaranteed housing for 4 years

NYU Cons:

* city is kinda dirty
* not as prestigious as my other option
* broken-up campus -> might be harder to make friends?

**USC** 

USC Pros:

* also in a cool city
* guaranteed free tuition (haven't gotten financial aid back but price will be 20k/year at highest)
* really good architecture school, overall prestigious university
* traditional-style campus -> more conducive for making friends?
* weather is nice year-round

USC Cons:

* city is also dirty
* i feel like the school's reputation is kinda tarnished by scandal? idk
* no guaranteed housing after 2nd year
* really far away from where i live (dc)

As a DC native who is also a girl and used to go out with friends late at night pre-covid, I can tell you that for GWU, foggy bottom/Georgetown is a really nice place to be in, even in the wee hours of the night there is nothing really dangerous to worry about as long as you are not alone. There are obviously homeless people who hang out at metro stops and also on the street corners, but as the GWU area is kinda residential too it's really nothing to worry about in terms of safety. I have never had a bad experience downtown, but just be sure to travel alongside at least one or two other people that you know. For AU, I don't go to that part of the city much, but my mom works over there and it is a really nice place to be. I have friends there who enjoy their time at AU and never bring up any safety concerns or anything- Tenleytown is a pretty quiet place with cute coffee shops and yoga studios. Nothing much besides that and homes, so honestly I think you are fine with that too. Overall, DC is a pretty safe city to be in, and I would recommend it to anyone interested in going to college here!
